utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please sit down. Good afternoon. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-02-60/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Momir Nikolic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Nikolic, can you hear the proceedings and understand them? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the appearances, please. Let's start with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution is myself, Norman Farrell, and with me is appeals counsel, Mr. Marcussen and Ms. Kind. Our case manager is Ms. Galicia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TANSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, good afternoon. Appearing for Mr. Nikolic, my name is Rock Tansey, and Mr. Livingston is my co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. [Interpretation] Pursuant to Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, a Status Conference shall be convened within 120 days after the Notice of Appeal was filed and then within 120 days after the last Status Conference in order to allow everyone to raise issues that concern the appeals procedure. This is the fifth Status Conference in relation to the appeal filed by Mr. Nikolic. Mr. Nikolic or his counsel, would you like to raise any issues that concern the detention conditions or your mental or physical health?

utterances.speaker: MR. TANSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no observations to make. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] As far as how the appeals procedure is progressing is concerned, the purpose of this Status Conference is to examine how the case is proceeding. This case has been affected by the withdrawal of two of the lead counsels and by the recent appointment of co- counsel, Mr. Livingston, who is assisting Mr. Tansey. Since the beginning of the appeals proceedings, we have run into a certain number of difficulties that have considerably delayed the appeal proceedings. In the light of these most recent events, I am certain that the parties will now be in a position to fully focus on Mr. Nikolic's appeal. The Appeals Chamber has ruled on the most recent motions filed by the Defence. The motions concerned are the following ones: The request to withdraw motions to admit additional evidence and the motion to amend the Notice of Appeal filed on the 6th of June, 2005, which also contains a request to file a revised appellant's brief. Secondly, we have the motion to amend the Notice of Appeal that was filed on the 29th of June, 2005. The Appeals Chamber has decided to grant the three motions filed by Mr. Nikolic and hereby authorises the following: Firstly, the withdrawal of the two motions that were filed on the 23rd of December, 2004. Secondly, the filing of the appellant's brief, the purpose of which is to clarify the current brief. Thirdly, the filing of a new Notice of Appeal in which the erroneous references under paragraph 1(b) will be replaced by the correct ones. The following deadline has been established for the filing of the new written submissions: Mr. Nikolic will have to file his new Notice of Appeal by Friday, the 22nd of July, 2005, at the latest. The revised appellant's brief should be filed by Monday, the 8th of August, 2005, at the latest. If necessary, an amended respondent's brief may be filed by the Prosecution no later than Friday, the 26th of August, 2005. A brief in reply, a revised brief in reply, may also be filed by Monday, the 5th of September, 2005, at the latest. I would like to invite the parties to take advantage of the filings of these revised written submissions in order to include all necessary corrections in their briefs. At this point in time, I would also like to invite the parties to fully respect the schedule established. A written decision concerning this disposition as well as the motives of the Appeals Chamber will now be handed out to you by the registrar, and I thank him in advance for his assistance. As far as I am concerned, I have no other comments to make at this Status Conference. Do the parties have any comments they would like to make or any issues they would like to raise? Mr. Tansey.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it purely relates to the third order that you've made for, if need be, a revised brief in reply shall be filed no later than Monday, the 5th of September, 2005. The position is that I, in fact, will -- will be away on vacation until the end of August, so it may be that the 5th of September is possibly too swift for a reply. If I was to ask for, for example, the 12th of September, which is giving an extra week, I would hope that that should be sufficient. Regarding the other matters, we have no observation to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Tansey, this is the Appeals Chamber decision, naturally, and the Pre-Trial Judge or the Pre-Appeal Judge cannot change this. Secondly, I think that the Appeals Chamber has already taken into consideration certain factors that have delayed the proceedings and, I noted it before, fixing this deadline. Mr. Tansey, with the assistance of Mr. Livingston - and I do apologise - you could perhaps reach an agreement and try to respect the deadline that has already been set.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I say, certainly, we shall seek to honour the deadline. It's effectively that having agreed or drafted the document, we then have to get it translated for Mr. Nikolic, and -- and that adds to the delay. And that's why -- the only reason why, we suggest, that if we had the extra week, it may enable us to deal with all the matters in question. That's why we suggest, as well, if it could be changed to the 12th of September. Your Honour, I have nothing else to add to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, if you're about to address Mr. Tansey. The scheduling does affect the Prosecution, so I wanted to just inform you that I had a few comments on the scheduling before you addressed Mr. Tansey, as your answer may be the same for -- for both of us, which is that if it's the full Appeals Chamber that has to decide it, I was going to -- well, I can wait till Your Honour responds to Mr. Tansey or indicate the Prosecution's position, as you wish. If you'd like me to proceed with comments in that regard, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, would you like me to wait until I've answered the Defence counsel first.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tansey, I think you could seek to honour the deadline and, if need be, you could apply for a change with the Appeals Chamber, and we'll see what we can do. [In English] Let's do it like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm happy to do that. It's just, I thought, possibly avoid an unnecessary application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Farrell.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Merci. Thank you. In light of your suggestion, I was going to simply indicate that if and when we -- when we receive the revised appellate's brief, if there is any difficulty in filing our brief in 15 working days, we will simply inform the Court and set out a request, if necessary. If not, we will try and comply with the order. The only difficulty the Prosecution faces is, in the same period of time we have the Brdjanin brief, the Blagojevic brief. It's the summer recess, and we had maybe erroneously anticipated that we would have 40 days to file a response brief, as the appellant has had almost 70. So we were going under the original Rules. And since this matter was scheduled, I didn't anticipate the necessity of doing this so expeditiously. But I take Your Honour's comments. We will receive the brief, take a look at it when we receive it, and try and comply with the order. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the Appeals Chamber has taken into account the fact that there were many delays, I believe we're going to maintain things as they are. And if the need arises in the future, you will file an application and we shall decide accordingly. Do you have any other questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANSEY
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, since there are no questions, the Status Conference is adjourned. It is so decided.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
